Proof Debt Ledger

Auto-generated by (proof-debt-ledger). 990 proven theorem(s); each is certified by the kernel relative to the asserted facts listed as its outstanding base.

Reading an entry

A proof's bill is the set of asserted facts it ultimately leans on -- resolved transitively: a cited proven lemma contributes its own bill, a primitive axiom or definitional fact contributes nothing, and an asserted fact contributes itself. Each such fact is a leaf of the bill.

  • proven modulo 0 (an empty bill) -- the proof rests only on the trusted base (the fixed primitive axioms, the kernel inference rules, and definitions). Nothing asserted stands between it and the kernel; this is the strongest thing a proof can report, and it carries no trust tier.
  • proven modulo {a, b, ...} -- the proof is unconditional given a, b, ... Discharging every leaf (proving it, or making it a definition) would collapse the bill to 0.

The trust tier [trust: K] of a non-empty bill is the warrant of its weakest leaf -- one shaky leaf caps the whole proof. Tiers, weakest to strongest (from *warrant-kinds*; see the manual, ch. Classification):

| tier | the weakest leaf is... | |------|------------------------| | none | asserted with no warrant at all -- a backlog item, not a category | | hand-wave | a heuristic / plausibility argument, not rigorous | | well-known | a standard textbook fact, asserted without argument | | reference | cites a specific named source | | informal | a rigorous paper-proof exists, just not mechanised in VNB | | proof | a machine-checked VNB proof exists |

So [trust: none] is the weakest report (some leaf justifies nothing), and modulo 0 -- no tier -- is the strongest.

Forward: proven theorem -> outstanding base

bdd-metric-converges-fwd (trust: well-known)

trusted code: ineq -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

  • bdd-metric-is-metric-space -- warrant well-known: rho = d/(1+d) is a metric. Nonnegativity, symmetry and the zero law come from d via the increasing map f(t)=t/(1+t) (bdd-fn-nonneg, bdd-fn-mono, and f(t)=0 iff t=0); the triangle inequality is f's subadditivity (bdd-fn-subadd) composed with monotonicity over d's triangle inequality.
  • bdd-metric-carrier -- warrant well-known: BDD-METRIC keeps the point set: PTS(BDD-METRIC s) = PTS(s). Read off the functoid (the carrier slot is (PTS s) verbatim).
  • bdd-metric-distance -- warrant well-known: Beta-reduction of the BDD-METRIC distance lambda: rho(x,y) = d(x,y)/(1+d(x,y)).
  • bdd-fn-le-arg -- warrant well-known: t/(1+t) <= t for t >= 0: equivalent to t <= t*(1+t) = t + t^2, i.e. 0 <= t^2. Gives one half of the topological equivalence d/(1+d) ~ d (the identity from (X,d) to (X, d/(1+d)) is 1-Lipschitz, hence continuous).

  • bdd-metric-is-metric-space -- warrant well-known: rho = d/(1+d) is a metric. Nonnegativity, symmetry and the zero law come from d via the increasing map f(t)=t/(1+t) (bdd-fn-nonneg, bdd-fn-mono, and f(t)=0 iff t=0); the triangle inequality is f's subadditivity (bdd-fn-subadd) composed with monotonicity over d's triangle inequality.
  • bdd-metric-carrier -- warrant well-known: BDD-METRIC keeps the point set: PTS(BDD-METRIC s) = PTS(s). Read off the functoid (the carrier slot is (PTS s) verbatim).
  • bdd-metric-bounded -- warrant well-known: rho(x,y) = d/(1+d) < 1 always (bdd-fn-lt-one): the bounded metric has diameter at most 1, whatever the diameter of (X,d).

The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

  • bt-succ-in-nn -- warrant well-known: succ closes NN.
  • bt-nn-in-zz -- warrant well-known: NN subset ZZ.

  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

TWO THINGS BLOCK THE MECHANIZATION, and neither is the mathematics. (1) is-norm's FIRST conjunct is abs in FUN(CARR, RR)' -- membership in a function SPACE, not the pointwise typing rr-abs-closed gives. abs' is a primitive operator, i.e. a class function; that its restriction to RR is a SET is a replacement/sethood obligation, and nothing in the tree states it for abs (nor for `magnitude', which puts cc-is-normed-field in exactly the same position). (2) LOAD ORDER: rr-abs-basics.scm is a theorem-library file and loads some 900 entries after this one, so the proof cannot live where the axiom is cited from; retiring the axiom means moving the citation site, the way zz-is-integral-domain was moved.

  • comb-kk-in-fun -- warrant well-known: Each COMB-KK(R,x,y,m) is a total function ZZ -> CARR R: base is IF into {ONE,ZERO}; step is a sum of products of carrier elements. Induction on m.
  • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • mvt-aux-cont -- warrant reference: h is a sum/product of f, constants and the identity, hence continuous where f is.
  • mvt-aux-diff -- warrant reference: h=(b-a)f-(f(b)-f(a))id is a linear combination of f and identity; its derivative (b-a)L-(f(b)-f(a)) follows from deriv-product/sum/const/identity.
  • max-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(a)<h(c) => a<c<b (a strict max above equal endpoints is interior).
  • rr-prod-nonpos-pos -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v>0 forces u<=0.
  • rr-prod-nonpos-neg -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v<0 forces u>=0.
  • continuous-nonpos-right -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is <=0 on a right-neighborhood (th,bb) is <=0 at th (sign preservation under continuity / one-sided limit).
  • continuous-nonneg-left -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is >=0 at th.
  • min-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(c)<h(a) => a<c<b.
  • deriv-neg -- warrant reference: Derivative of -f is -f': f(x)-f(a)=phi(x)(x-a) gives (-f)(x)-(-f)(a) = (-phi)(x)(x-a), with -phi continuous at a and value -L.
  • rr-midpoint-between -- warrant well-known: a<b => exists m with a<m<b.
  • diff-value-real -- warrant informal: IS-DIFF-AT's definition includes (IN L RR) as a conjunct.
  • cont-agree-off-pt -- warrant well-known: fa, fb continuous at pt and fa(x)=fb(x) for all x/=pt => fa(pt)=fb(pt). pt is a limit point of RR (no isolated points), so both values are the common limit of the punctured values; take x -> pt.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form. Rigorous from the axioms present since order completeness landed (rr-sup-in / rr-sup-upper / rr-sup-least, number-systems.scm): if NN had an upper bound it would have a least one, s = SUP(NN); s - 1 is then not an upper bound, so s - 1 < n for some natural n, so s < n + 1, and n + 1 is a natural. Not mechanised -- that is the driver this warrant is standing in for.
  • bt-neg1-in-zz -- warrant well-known: -1 in ZZ.
  • bt-neg1-neg -- warrant well-known: -1 < 0.
  • bt-succ-minus-1 -- warrant well-known: succ n - 1 = n in ZZ.
  • comb-kk-above -- warrant well-known: k>m => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base k>0 => IF(k=0) is ZERO; step k>succ m => both k-1>m and k>m, ZERO by IH.
  • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.
  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.
  • bt-one-in-carr -- warrant well-known: ring ONE lies in CARR.
  • comb-kk-0-0 -- warrant well-known: comb-kk-zero + IF(0=0) picks the then-branch ONE(R).
  • bt-succ-in-nn -- warrant well-known: succ closes NN.
  • bt-nn-in-zz -- warrant well-known: NN subset ZZ.
  • bt-sum-in-carr-zz -- warrant well-known: SUM over the NN indices of a ZZ-fn lands in CARR.
  • bt-lt-succ -- warrant well-known: n < succ n.
  • ring-power-zero -- warrant informal: mpow-zero: MPOW(m,x,0)=IDEN(m); the view's E|->ONE slot gives IDEN(COMMUTATIVE-RING-MULTIPLICATIVE-CM R)=(ONE R).

  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

TWO THINGS BLOCK THE MECHANIZATION, and neither is the mathematics.   • elem-g-entry-l-at-k -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{kc} = r when c=l and k/=l (the r-slot in column l).
  • elem-g-entry-off-l-off-diag -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{jc} = 0 when c/=l and j/=c (off the diagonal, off the r-slot).
  • elem-g-entry-off-l-diag -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{cc} = 1 when c/=l (the diagonal, r-slot inactive).
  • entry-of-identmat -- warrant reference: (IDENTMAT A n)_{ij} = 1 if i=j else 0 (entry-of-matof on the Kronecker delta).
  • elem-g-col-l -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{il} = 1 if i=l, r if i=k, else 0 (column l: diagonal + the r-slot).
  • elem-g-col-k -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{ik} = 1 if i=k else 0, when k/=l (column k is an identity column).
  • ring-one-in -- warrant well-known: ONE lies in the carrier.
  • ring-add-right-id -- warrant well-known: a + 0 = a (ring-add-left-id + comm).
  • ring-add-right-inv -- warrant well-known: a + (-a) = 0 (ring-add-left-inv + comm).
  • elem-g-col-other -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{ic} = 1 if i=c else 0, when c/=l (any non-l column is identity).
  • ring-neg-neg -- warrant well-known: -(-r) = r in any ring: r's additive inverse's inverse is r (group double-inverse).
  • nn-succ-le-antisym -- warrant well-known: succ a <= b => not(b <= a) for a,b in NN: succ a <= b gives a < b, so b <= a would give a < a. Elementary order on NN.

Nonnegativity, symmetry and the zero law are termwise (D_w(x,y)=0 iff every weighted term is 0 iff rho_n=0 iff x(n)=y(n) for all n iff x=y, as w(n)>0). The triangle inequality is the sum over n of the per-factor bounded triangle inequalities (each rho_n is a metric, bdd-metric-is-metric-space), the sums converging by product-weighted-summable.
  • seq-compact-countable-product -- warrant reference: Given a sequence seq in the product carrier (= PTS(PRODUCT-METRIC ms), by product-metric-carrier), coordinatewise-diagonal-subseq yields a strictly monotone delta and L in PRODUCT-CARRIER(ms) with SUBSEQ(seq,delta) converging in every coordinate to L(n). product-convergence-coordinatewise -- at the default summable weights (product-metric-default-summable) -- turns coordinatewise convergence into CONVERGES-TO(PRODUCT-METRIC ms, SUBSEQ(seq,delta), L). So every product sequence has a convergent subsequence: PRODUCT-METRIC(ms) is sequentially compact.

Hence f converges to x. This is the standard fact powering compact => complete (calculus.pdf Prop 3.12).

Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

TWO THINGS BLOCK THE MECHANIZATION, and neither is the mathematics. (1) is-norm's FIRST conjunct is abs in FUN(CARR, RR)' -- membership in a function SPACE, not the pointwise typing rr-abs-closed gives. abs' is a primitive operator, i.e. a class function; that its restriction to RR is a SET is a replacement/sethood obligation, and nothing in the tree states it for abs (nor for `magnitude', which puts cc-is-normed-field in exactly the same position). (2) LOAD ORDER: rr-abs-basics.scm is a theorem-library file and loads some 900 entries after this one, so the proof cannot live where the axiom is cited from; retiring the axiom means moving the citation site, the way zz-is-integral-domain was moved.

No inverses used -- the same argument as finsum-comm-monoid-type.
  • mvag-carr -- warrant proof: carrier of a module's vector abelian group is the module's vector set.
  • matact-type -- warrant reference: P.u is an m-by-q matrix of vectors for P an m-by-n scalar matrix and u an n-by-q matrix of vectors: matof-in-mat, whose values are FINSUMs in the vector abelian group, typed by finsum-type + mvag-carr.
  • abelian-group-right-id -- warrant well-known: a * e = e * a = a, by abelian-group-opr-comm then group-left-id (via abelian-group-is-group).

proven modulo:

  • nn-finite-subset-bounded -- warrant well-known: A finite subset T of NN is bounded. By finite-set-induction (cardinality.scm, primitive) on T: the empty set is bounded by N = 0, and if T is bounded by N then T u {x} is bounded by max(succ x, N) (nn-pair-upper-bound, order-lemmas). Hence some N in NN has y < N for every y in T, so no y >= N is in T. The contrapositive of `inf-subset-nn-unbounded' (diagonalization-lemmas.scm), which asserts the same equivalence from the other side and is warranted the same way. Not mechanised: the induction runs over a COMP class { T | T subset NN => bounded } and wants the comprehension-membership bookkeeping, sethood of T, and the max-of-two-naturals brick threaded through -- routine, and no library payoff beyond this one citation.
  • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.
  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.
  • nn-pos-is-succ -- warrant well-known: a positive nat is a successor (n>=1 => n = succ(n-1), n-1 in NN).

log-above-any (trust: well-known)

trusted code: crs, ineq, arith, sos -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

  • mvt-aux-cont -- warrant reference: h is a sum/product of f, constants and the identity, hence continuous where f is.
  • mvt-aux-diff -- warrant reference: h=(b-a)f-(f(b)-f(a))id is a linear combination of f and identity; its derivative (b-a)L-(f(b)-f(a)) follows from deriv-product/sum/const/identity.
  • max-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(a)<h(c) => a<c<b (a strict max above equal endpoints is interior).
  • rr-prod-nonpos-pos -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v>0 forces u<=0.
  • rr-prod-nonpos-neg -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v<0 forces u>=0.
  • continuous-nonpos-right -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is <=0 on a right-neighborhood (th,bb) is <=0 at th (sign preservation under continuity / one-sided limit).
  • continuous-nonneg-left -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is >=0 at th.
  • min-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(c)<h(a) => a<c<b.
  • deriv-neg -- warrant reference: Derivative of -f is -f': f(x)-f(a)=phi(x)(x-a) gives (-f)(x)-(-f)(a) = (-phi)(x)(x-a), with -phi continuous at a and value -L.
  • rr-midpoint-between -- warrant well-known: a<b => exists m with a<m<b.
  • diff-value-real -- warrant informal: IS-DIFF-AT's definition includes (IN L RR) as a conjunct.
  • cont-agree-off-pt -- warrant well-known: fa, fb continuous at pt and fa(x)=fb(x) for all x/=pt => fa(pt)=fb(pt). pt is a limit point of RR (no isolated points), so both values are the common limit of the punctured values; take x -> pt.
  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

TWO THINGS BLOCK THE MECHANIZATION, and neither is the mathematics. (1) is-norm's FIRST conjunct is abs in FUN(CARR, RR)' -- membership in a function SPACE, not the pointwise typing rr-abs-closed gives. abs' is a primitive operator, i.e. a class function; that its restriction to RR is a SET is a replacement/sethood obligation, and nothing in the tree states it for abs (nor for `magnitude', which puts cc-is-normed-field in exactly the same position). (2) LOAD ORDER: rr-abs-basics.scm is a theorem-library file and loads some 900 entries after this one, so the proof cannot live where the axiom is cited from; retiring the axiom means moving the citation site, the way zz-is-integral-domain was moved.

  • comb-kk-in-fun -- warrant well-known: Each COMB-KK(R,x,y,m) is a total function ZZ -> CARR R: base is IF into {ONE,ZERO}; step is a sum of products of carrier elements. Induction on m.
  • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form. Rigorous from the axioms present since order completeness landed (rr-sup-in / rr-sup-upper / rr-sup-least, number-systems.scm): if NN had an upper bound it would have a least one, s = SUP(NN); s - 1 is then not an upper bound, so s - 1 < n for some natural n, so s < n + 1, and n + 1 is a natural. Not mechanised -- that is the driver this warrant is standing in for.
  • bt-neg1-in-zz -- warrant well-known: -1 in ZZ.
  • bt-neg1-neg -- warrant well-known: -1 < 0.
  • bt-succ-minus-1 -- warrant well-known: succ n - 1 = n in ZZ.
  • comb-kk-above -- warrant well-known: k>m => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base k>0 => IF(k=0) is ZERO; step k>succ m => both k-1>m and k>m, ZERO by IH.
  • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.
  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.
  • bt-one-in-carr -- warrant well-known: ring ONE lies in CARR.
  • comb-kk-0-0 -- warrant well-known: comb-kk-zero + IF(0=0) picks the then-branch ONE(R).
  • bt-succ-in-nn -- warrant well-known: succ closes NN.
  • bt-nn-in-zz -- warrant well-known: NN subset ZZ.
  • bt-sum-in-carr-zz -- warrant well-known: SUM over the NN indices of a ZZ-fn lands in CARR.
  • bt-lt-succ -- warrant well-known: n < succ n.
  • ring-power-zero -- warrant informal: mpow-zero: MPOW(m,x,0)=IDEN(m); the view's E|->ONE slot gives IDEN(COMMUTATIVE-RING-MULTIPLICATIVE-CM R)=(ONE R).

Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

  • comb-kk-in-fun -- warrant well-known: Each COMB-KK(R,x,y,m) is a total function ZZ -> CARR R: base is IF into {ONE,ZERO}; step is a sum of products of carrier elements. Induction on m.
  • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form. Rigorous from the axioms present since order completeness landed (rr-sup-in / rr-sup-upper / rr-sup-least, number-systems.scm): if NN had an upper bound it would have a least one, s = SUP(NN); s - 1 is then not an upper bound, so s - 1 < n for some natural n, so s < n + 1, and n + 1 is a natural.   • bt-succ-minus-1 -- warrant well-known: succ n - 1 = n in ZZ.
  • comb-kk-above -- warrant well-known: k>m => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base k>0 => IF(k=0) is ZERO; step k>succ m => both k-1>m and k>m, ZERO by IH.

  • comb-kk-0-0 -- warrant well-known: comb-kk-zero + IF(0=0) picks the then-branch ONE(R).

  • bt-nn-in-zz -- warrant well-known: NN subset ZZ.
  • bt-sum-in-carr-zz -- warrant well-known: SUM over the NN indices of a ZZ-fn lands in CARR.
  • bt-lt-succ -- warrant well-known: n < succ n.
  • ring-power-zero -- warrant informal: mpow-zero: MPOW(m,x,0)=IDEN(m); the view's E|->ONE slot gives IDEN(COMMUTATIVE-RING-MULTIPLICATIVE-CM R)=(ONE R).

Hence B(s,a,delta) subset PREIMAGE(s,f,V): the preimage is open.

proven modulo:

  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.
  • card-subset-nn -- warrant well-known: A subset of a finite set is finite (its cardinality is bounded by the superset's). Standard; the RHS terms PROD-RING(R,a,S) and PROD-RING(R,b,X\S) need S and X\S finite to be well-defined.
  • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.
  • nn-finite-subset-bounded -- warrant well-known: A finite subset T of NN is bounded. By finite-set-induction (cardinality.scm, primitive) on T: the empty set is bounded by N = 0, and if T is bounded by N then T u {x} is bounded by max(succ x, N) (nn-pair-upper-bound, order-lemmas). Hence some N in NN has y < N for every y in T, so no y >= N is in T. The contrapositive of `inf-subset-nn-unbounded' (diagonalization-lemmas.scm), which asserts the same equivalence from the other side and is warranted the same way. Not mechanised: the induction runs over a COMP class { T | T subset NN => bounded } and wants the comprehension-membership bookkeeping, sethood of T, and the max-of-two-naturals brick threaded through -- routine, and no library payoff beyond this one citation.

proven modulo:

  • dual-norm-is-bound -- warrant reference: The operator norm DUAL-NORM(m,f) satisfies |f(x)| <= ||f|| ||x|| for every x (it is defined as the least such bound; in particular it IS a bound).
  • vnrm-nonneg -- warrant reference: Norm nonnegativity, a defining law of IS-NORMED-VECTOR-SPACE.
  • bdd-linfun-abs-real -- warrant reference: A bounded linear functional maps VEC(m) into RR, so |f(x)| is a real.
  • dual-norm-nonneg -- warrant reference: DUAL-NORM is defined by IOTA over c in RR with 0<=c, so for a bounded f it is a nonnegative real.
  • le-bound-mono -- warrant well-known: Reals: from p<=an, a<=b and 0<=n, scale a<=b by n>=0 to an<=b*n, then transitivity gives p<=b*n.
  • line-functional-exists -- warrant reference: On the one-dimensional subspace RR.v the map r.v |-> r.||v|| is a bounded linear functional of operator norm <= 1 (=1 for v/=0) taking the value ||v|| at v; for v=0 the zero functional serves.
  • line-is-submodule -- warrant reference: RR.v is the image of the scalar action, closed under addition, negation and the action, and contains 0 = 0.v; so it is a submodule.
  • vspace-vec-is-set -- warrant reference: The carrier VEC(m) of a vector space (module) is a set.
  • good-sub-submodule -- warrant reference: GOOD-SUB unfolds to NPE, whose first conjunct is IS-SUBMODULE m t.
  • good-sub-self -- warrant reference: f is a norm-preserving extension of itself to s (bound = ||f||_s), so s is reachable.
  • good-sub-in-power -- warrant reference: A reachable t is a submodule, hence a subset of VEC(m), hence in its powerset.
  • dc-on-nn-pred -- warrant reference: Set-valued-step form of dc-on-nn (same file). Derivable from primitive recursion on NN + global Hilbert choice: g(k,u):=CHOICE{y in X:y in nxt (k,u)} is defined by the totality hypothesis, then recurse f(0):=a, f(succ k):=g(k,f k); f:NN->X by induction. No relation-set encoding -- nxt(k,u) is the successor SET, supplied as a VNB-LAMBDA, so callers avoid the (LIST k u y)-in-R comprehension/sethood/NTH plumbing (O1 of archive/calculus-pre-rename/block-family-rederive.scm). Accepted asserted during library-build.
  • fun-codomain-superset -- warrant well-known: A function into B is a function into any superset C (fun-codomain-iff + subset-mem).
  • submodule-subset -- warrant reference: A submodule is by definition a subset of the vectors.
  • proper-subset-witness -- warrant well-known: If a subset b but a != b then by extensionality some x in b is not in a.
  • dual-norm-on-nonneg -- warrant reference: DUAL-NORM-ON is defined by IOTA over c in RR with 0<=c, so for a bounded functional it is a nonnegative real.
  • hb-gap -- warrant reference: Hahn-Banach gap (real, one dimension): with M = ||f||_s, for z,w in s f(w-z) <= M||w-z|| <= M(||z+v||+||w+v||), so sup_z(-f(z)-M||z+v||) <= inf_w(-f(w)+M||w+v||); RR order-completeness gives a separating alpha, whence |f(y)+r.alpha| <= M||y+r.v|| for all y in s, r in RR.
  • hb-extend-construct -- warrant reference: Extending a linear functional one dimension: with v notin s every element of s + RR.v is uniquely y + r.v, so g(y+r.v) = f(y) + r.alpha is a well-defined linear functional on s + RR.v extending f, for any scalar alpha. Standard linear algebra; alpha is fixed only by the bound (hb-gap).
  • span-add-one-membership -- warrant proof: Separation membership: SPAN-ADD-ONE(m,s,v) = SEP(w in VEC(m) | exists y in s, r in RR. w = y + r.v); a member iff in VEC(m) and it so decomposes.
  • span-add-one-submodule -- warrant reference: t + RR.v is closed under addition, negation and the scalar action and contains 0, so it is a submodule.
  • span-add-one-superset -- warrant reference: Every y in t equals y + 0.v, so t is contained in t + RR.v.
  • extends-on-trans -- warrant reference: If g2=g1 on t, g1=f on s, and s subset t, then g2=f on s.
  • linfun-app-abs-real -- warrant reference: A linear functional on t maps into RR, so |g(w)| is a real for w in t.
  • dual-norm-on-le-bound -- warrant reference: DUAL-NORM-ON(m,s,g) is the least c>=0 bounding |g(w)| by c*||w|| on s (IOTA least-upper-bound), hence <= any such bound c.
  • span-add-one-has-v -- warrant reference: v = 0 + 1.v with 0 in t, so v is in t + RR.v.
  • vec-is-set -- warrant reference: VEC(m) in SET, a defining clause of IS-NORMED-VECTOR-SPACE (definedness).
  • linfun-on-vec-is-linfun -- warrant reference: IS-LINEAR-FUNCTIONAL-ON m (VEC m) f and IS-LINEAR-FUNCTIONAL m f unfold to the same conjunction (f in FUN(VEC m,RR), additive, homogeneous over VEC m).
  • dual-norm-le-bound -- warrant reference: DUAL-NORM(m,f) is the least c>=0 bounding |f(w)| by c*||w|| on VEC(m) (IOTA least-upper-bound), hence <= any such bound c.
  • line-has-v -- warrant reference: v = 1.v, so v is in RR.v = LINE(m,v).
  • abs-nonneg-le -- warrant well-known: For a real a >= 0, |a| = a, so |a| <= c gives a <= c.

  • hb-gap -- warrant reference: Hahn-Banach gap (real, one dimension): with M = ||f||_s, for z,w in s f(w-z) <= M||w-z|| <= M(||z+v||+||w+v||), so sup_z(-f(z)-M||z+v||) <= inf_w(-f(w)+M||w+v||); RR order-completeness gives a separating alpha, whence |f(y)+r.alpha| <= M||y+r.v|| for all y in s, r in RR.
  • hb-extend-construct -- warrant reference: Extending a linear functional one dimension: with v notin s every element of s + RR.v is uniquely y + r.v, so g(y+r.v) = f(y) + r.alpha is a well-defined linear functional on s + RR.v extending f, for any scalar alpha. Standard linear algebra; alpha is fixed only by the bound (hb-gap).
  • span-add-one-membership -- warrant proof: Separation membership: SPAN-ADD-ONE(m,s,v) = SEP(w in VEC(m) | exists y in s, r in RR. w = y + r.v); a member iff in VEC(m) and it so decomposes.
  • span-add-one-submodule -- warrant reference: t + RR.v is closed under addition, negation and the scalar action and contains 0, so it is a submodule.
  • span-add-one-superset -- warrant reference: Every y in t equals y + 0.v, so t is contained in t + RR.v.
  • extends-on-trans -- warrant reference: If g2=g1 on t, g1=f on s, and s subset t, then g2=f on s.
  • vnrm-nonneg -- warrant reference: Norm nonnegativity, a defining law of IS-NORMED-VECTOR-SPACE.
  • linfun-app-abs-real -- warrant reference: A linear functional on t maps into RR, so |g(w)| is a real for w in t.
  • dual-norm-on-le-bound -- warrant reference: DUAL-NORM-ON(m,s,g) is the least c>=0 bounding |g(w)| by c*||w|| on s (IOTA least-upper-bound), hence <= any such bound c.
  • le-bound-mono -- warrant well-known: Reals: from p<=an, a<=b and 0<=n, scale a<=b by n>=0 to an<=b*n, then transitivity gives p<=b*n.
  • span-add-one-has-v -- warrant reference: v = 0 + 1.v with 0 in t, so v is in t + RR.v.
  • vec-is-set -- warrant reference: VEC(m) in SET, a defining clause of IS-NORMED-VECTOR-SPACE (definedness).
  • linfun-on-vec-is-linfun -- warrant reference: IS-LINEAR-FUNCTIONAL-ON m (VEC m) f and IS-LINEAR-FUNCTIONAL m f unfold to the same conjunction (f in FUN(VEC m,RR), additive, homogeneous over VEC m).
  • dual-norm-le-bound -- warrant reference: DUAL-NORM(m,f) is the least c>=0 bounding |f(w)| by c*||w|| on VEC(m) (IOTA least-upper-bound), hence <= any such bound c.
  • dual-norm-nonneg -- warrant reference: DUAL-NORM is defined by IOTA over c in RR with 0<=c, so for a bounded f it is a nonnegative real.
  • line-has-v -- warrant reference: v = 1.v, so v is in RR.v = LINE(m,v).
  • gof-in-fun -- warrant reference: g : VEC(m) -> RR (bounded linear functional) composed with f : RR -> VEC(m) is g o f : RR -> RR.
  • gof-taylor-diff -- warrant reference: A bounded linear functional g is linear and continuous, so it commutes with the Caratheodory derivative: if f^(k) is norm-continuous / vector-differentiable with factor phi, then (g o f)^(k) = g o f^(k) is continuous / differentiable with factor g o phi. Hence g o f is scalar-Taylor-differentiable to order n.
  • taylor-g-in-fun -- warrant reference: G(t)=f(x)-TAYLOR-POLY(f,t,n,x) maps RR to RR (finite sum of products of reals), for each degree n in NN.
  • taylor-h-in-fun -- warrant reference: H(t)=(x-t)^(n+1) maps RR to RR, for each degree n in NN.
  • taylor-gmvt-cont -- warrant reference: G and H are continuous on [a,x]: H is a polynomial, G a finite sum of products of the continuous derivatives f^(k) with polynomials (taylor-G-cont/H-cont).
  • taylor-gmvt-diff -- warrant reference: G and H are differentiable at every real point of (a,x) (taylor-G-diff/H-diff give the explicit derivatives), so each has SOME derivative there.
  • gmvt-aux-cont -- warrant reference: h = (g(b)-g(a))f - (f(b)-f(a))g is a linear combination of f and g, hence continuous wherever both f and g are (calculus.pdf Thm 2.11).
  • gmvt-aux-diff -- warrant reference: h'(x) = (g(b)-g(a))f'(x) - (f(b)-f(a))g'(x), from deriv-sum/scalar-mult on the linear combination h = (g(b)-g(a))f - (f(b)-f(a))g (calculus.pdf Thm 2.11).
  • max-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(a)<h(c) => a<c<b (a strict max above equal endpoints is interior).
  • rr-prod-nonpos-pos -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v>0 forces u<=0.
  • rr-prod-nonpos-neg -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v<0 forces u>=0.
  • continuous-nonpos-right -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is <=0 on a right-neighborhood (th,bb) is <=0 at th (sign preservation under continuity / one-sided limit).
  • continuous-nonneg-left -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is >=0 at th.
  • min-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(c)<h(a) => a<c<b.
  • deriv-neg -- warrant reference: Derivative of -f is -f': f(x)-f(a)=phi(x)(x-a) gives (-f)(x)-(-f)(a) = (-phi)(x)(x-a), with -phi continuous at a and value -L.
  • rr-midpoint-between -- warrant well-known: a<b => exists m with a<m<b.
  • diff-value-real -- warrant informal: IS-DIFF-AT's definition includes (IN L RR) as a conjunct.
  • cont-agree-off-pt -- warrant well-known: fa, fb continuous at pt and fa(x)=fb(x) for all x/=pt => fa(pt)=fb(pt). pt is a limit point of RR (no isolated points), so both values are the common limit of the punctured values; take x -> pt.
  • taylor-g-diff -- warrant reference: Telescoping: d/dt[f(x)-Sum_{k<=n} f^(k)(t)(x-t)^k/k!] = -(f^(n+1)(t)/n!)(x-t)^n. Differentiate term k by the product rule: the f^(k+1)(t)(x-t)^k/k! piece of term k cancels the -f^(k+1)(t)(x-t)^k/k! piece of term k+1, leaving only the last -(f^(n+1)(t)/n!)(x-t)^n. Standard (calculus.pdf Taylor section).
  • taylor-h-diff -- warrant reference: d/dt[(x-t)^(n+1)] = -(n+1)(x-t)^n (chain rule on the polynomial).
  • taylor-g-at-x -- warrant reference: G(x) = f(x) - TAYLOR-POLY(f,x,n,x) = f(x) - f(x) = 0 (taylor-poly-at-center).
  • taylor-g-at-a -- warrant reference: G(a) = f(x) - TAYLOR-POLY(f,a,n,x) (beta).
  • taylor-h-at-x -- warrant reference: H(x) = (x-x)^(n+1) = 0^(n+1) = 0.
  • taylor-h-at-a -- warrant reference: H(a) = (x-a)^(n+1) (beta).
  • rr-power-pos -- warrant well-known: 0<d gives 0<d^n for every n (induction: d^0=1>0; d^(n+1)=d*d^n, product of positives).
  • taylor-deriv-real -- warrant reference: f^(n+1)(t) is the derivative value of the differentiable f^(n) at t, hence real (IS-DIFF-AT carries its value in RR).
  • taylor-poly-in-rr -- warrant reference: TAYLOR-POLY is a finite sum of products of reals, hence real.
  • taylor-clear -- warrant well-known: Substitute gx=hx=0, ha=d, ga=r: (-(fn1/n!)pw)(-d) = (-(n+1)pw)(-r), i.e. (fn1/n!)pwd = (n+1)pwr; cancel pw/=0 and multiply by n! (using (n+1)*n! = (n+1)!) to get (n+1)! r = fn1 d. Pure real arithmetic.
  • g-of-remainder -- warrant reference: g linear: g(f(x) (-) p) = g(f(x)) - g(p) = (g o f)(x) - g(TAYLOR-POLY-V). g commutes with the finite VADD/ACT sum and with f^(k)(a), so g(TAYLOR-POLY-V(f,a,x,n)) = Sum ((x-a)^k/k!) g(f^(k)(a)) = Sum ((x-a)^k/k!) (g o f)^(k)(a) = TAYLOR-POLY(g o f, a, n, x).
  • gof-nth-deriv -- warrant reference: By induction on k using commutation 1's factor identity, (g o f)^(k) = g o f^(k) as functions; evaluating the (n+1)-st at t gives (g o f)^(n+1)(t) = g(f^(n+1)(t)).
  • nth-deriv-v-in-vec -- warrant reference: Each vector derivative f^(k) maps RR into VEC(m) (IS-DIFF-AT-V pins the value in VEC(m)); so f^(k)(t) is a vector.
  • blf-app-real -- warrant reference: A bounded linear functional g maps VEC(m) into RR, so g(v) is a real.
  • dual-norm-is-bound -- warrant reference: The operator norm DUAL-NORM(m,f) satisfies |f(x)| <= ||f|| ||x|| for every x (it is defined as the least such bound; in particular it IS a bound).
  • bdd-linfun-abs-real -- warrant reference: A bounded linear functional maps VEC(m) into RR, so |f(x)| is a real.
  • rr-mul-le-right -- warrant well-known: a<=b and 0<=c give ac <= bc.
  • nvs-act-one -- warrant reference: module-act-unital, act(one(scal(s)), x) = x, with ONE(SCAL m) = 1 -- rr-scalar-ring-one, slot 6 of the ring view of the instance tuple.

  • matmul-entry -- warrant reference: (P Q)_{ic} = sum_{j=1}^{n} P_{ij}*Q_{jc}, the product summed in A's additive group over j in 1..n (entry-of-matof on the MATMUL tabulation).
  • interval-card-in-nn -- warrant well-known: INTERVAL(a,b) with b in NN is finite, so its cardinality is a natural number.
  • matprod-summand-type -- warrant well-known: j |-> P_{ij}.Q_{jc} is a function [1,n] -> CARR A for P:MAT(m,n), Q:MAT(n,nn) (entry-in-carrier gives both factors in CARR A; MUL closes; CARR(RAG)=CARR A).
  • elem-g-entry-l-vanish -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{jc} = 0 when c=l and j is neither l (diagonal) nor k (r-slot).
  • ring-mul-zero-right -- warrant well-known: a.0 = 0: symmetric to ring-mul-zero-left. Lang, Algebra II.1.
  • ras-id -- warrant proof: identity of a ring's additive group is the ring's zero.
  • finsum-two-support -- warrant well-known: If f(j)=0 for every j in the finite S except j in {i0,i1} (i0/=i1), then FINSUM(ag,f,S) = f(i0) * f(i1) in ag.
  • elem-g-entry-l-at-l -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{lc} = 1 when c=l (the diagonal entry of column l).
  • elem-g-entry-l-at-k -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{kc} = r when c=l and k/=l (the r-slot in column l).
  • ras-op -- warrant proof: operation of a ring's additive group is the ring's addition.
  • elem-g-entry-off-l-off-diag -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{jc} = 0 when c/=l and j/=c (off the diagonal, off the r-slot).
  • finsum-single-support -- warrant well-known: If f(j)=0 for every j in the finite S except j=i0, then FINSUM(ag,f,S)=f(i0).
  • elem-g-entry-off-l-diag -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{cc} = 1 when c/=l (the diagonal, r-slot inactive).
  • matmul-type -- warrant reference: MAT(m,n,CARR A) x MAT(n,k,CARR A) -> MAT(m,k,CARR A): the tabulated product is a matrix whose entries are FINSUMs in the carrier (matof-in-mat + finsum-type).
  • identmat-type -- warrant reference: IDENTMAT(A,n) is an n-by-n matrix over CARR A (its entries are ONE/ZERO of A).
  • entry-of-identmat -- warrant reference: (IDENTMAT A n)_{ij} = 1 if i=j else 0 (entry-of-matof on the Kronecker delta).
  • elem-g-col-l -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{il} = 1 if i=l, r if i=k, else 0 (column l: diagonal + the r-slot).
  • elem-g-col-k -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{ik} = 1 if i=k else 0, when k/=l (column k is an identity column).
  • ring-mul-zero-left -- warrant well-known: 0.a = 0: a.0 = a.(0+0) = a.0 + a.0, cancel a.0 in the additive group. Lang, Algebra II.1.
  • ring-one-in -- warrant well-known: ONE lies in the carrier.
  • ring-add-right-id -- warrant well-known: a + 0 = a (ring-add-left-id + comm).
  • ring-add-right-inv -- warrant well-known: a + (-a) = 0 (ring-add-left-inv + comm).
  • elem-g-col-other -- warrant reference: G[r,k,l]_{ic} = 1 if i=c else 0, when c/=l (any non-l column is identity).
  • matrix-entry-extensionality -- warrant well-known: Two m-by-n matrices over X with equal entries are equal (tuple/list extensionality applied row- and entry-wise).
  • ring-neg-neg -- warrant well-known: -(-r) = r in any ring: r's additive inverse's inverse is r (group double-inverse).
  • identmat-left-identity -- warrant proof: I_m P = P: the (i,c) entry is sum_j delta_ij P_jc, whose only surviving term (j=i) is 1*P_ic = P_ic (matmul-entry + entry-of-identmat + finsum-single- support + ring-mul-left-id). Proof structure worked out in identmat-build.scm.
  • nn-succ-le-antisym -- warrant well-known: succ a <= b => not(b <= a) for a,b in NN: succ a <= b gives a < b, so b <= a would give a < a. Elementary order on NN.

trusted code: ineq -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

  • nn-finite-subset-bounded -- warrant well-known: A finite subset T of NN is bounded. By finite-set-induction (cardinality.scm, primitive) on T: the empty set is bounded by N = 0, and if T is bounded by N then T u {x} is bounded by max(succ x, N) (nn-pair-upper-bound, order-lemmas). Hence some N in NN has y < N for every y in T, so no y >= N is in T. The contrapositive of `inf-subset-nn-unbounded' (diagonalization-lemmas.scm), which asserts the same equivalence from the other side and is warranted the same way. Not mechanised: the induction runs over a COMP class { T | T subset NN => bounded } and wants the comprehension-membership bookkeeping, sethood of T, and the max-of-two-naturals brick threaded through -- routine, and no library payoff beyond this one citation.
  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.
  • card-subset-nn -- warrant well-known: A subset of a finite set is finite (its cardinality is bounded by the superset's). Standard; the RHS terms PROD-RING(R,a,S) and PROD-RING(R,b,X\S) need S and X\S finite to be well-defined.

product-convergence-coordinatewise (trust: well-known)

trusted code: crs, arith, ineq -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

  • product-is-metric-space -- warrant well-known: PRODUCT-METRIC-W(ms,w) is a metric space. Nonnegativity, symmetry and the zero law are termwise (D_w(x,y)=0 iff every weighted term is 0 iff rho_n=0 iff x(n)=y(n) for all n iff x=y, as w(n)>0). The triangle inequality is the sum over n of the per-factor bounded triangle inequalities (each rho_n is a metric, bdd-metric-is-metric-space), the sums converging by product-weighted-summable.
  • bdd-metric-is-metric-space -- warrant well-known: rho = d/(1+d) is a metric. Nonnegativity, symmetry and the zero law come from d via the increasing map f(t)=t/(1+t) (bdd-fn-nonneg, bdd-fn-mono, and f(t)=0 iff t=0); the triangle inequality is f's subadditivity (bdd-fn-subadd) composed with monotonicity over d's triangle inequality.
  • bdd-metric-carrier -- warrant well-known: BDD-METRIC keeps the point set: PTS(BDD-METRIC s) = PTS(s). Read off the functoid (the carrier slot is (PTS s) verbatim).
  • bdd-metric-bounded -- warrant well-known: rho(x,y) = d/(1+d) < 1 always (bdd-fn-lt-one): the bounded metric has diameter at most 1, whatever the diameter of (X,d).
  • bdd-metric-distance -- warrant well-known: Beta-reduction of the BDD-METRIC distance lambda: rho(x,y) = d(x,y)/(1+d(x,y)).
  • bdd-fn-le-arg -- warrant well-known: t/(1+t) <= t for t >= 0: equivalent to t <= t*(1+t) = t + t^2, i.e. 0 <= t^2. Gives one half of the topological equivalence d/(1+d) ~ d (the identity from (X,d) to (X, d/(1+d)) is 1-Lipschitz, hence continuous).

  • rr-prod-nonpos-neg -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v<0 forces u>=0.

  • continuous-nonneg-left -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is >=0 at th.

  • rr-midpoint-between -- warrant well-known: a<b => exists m with a<m<b.

  • cont-agree-off-pt -- warrant well-known: fa, fb continuous at pt and fa(x)=fb(x) for all x/=pt => fa(pt)=fb(pt). pt is a limit point of RR (no isolated points), so both values are the common limit of the punctured values; take x -> pt.
  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

TWO THINGS BLOCK THE MECHANIZATION, and neither is the mathematics. (1) is-norm's FIRST conjunct is abs in FUN(CARR, RR)' -- membership in a function SPACE, not the pointwise typing rr-abs-closed gives. abs' is a primitive operator, i.e. a class function; that its restriction to RR is a SET is a replacement/sethood obligation, and nothing in the tree states it for abs (nor for `magnitude', which puts cc-is-normed-field in exactly the same position). (2) LOAD ORDER: rr-abs-basics.scm is a theorem-library file and loads some 900 entries after this one, so the proof cannot live where the axiom is cited from; retiring the axiom means moving the citation site, the way zz-is-integral-domain was moved.

  • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form. Rigorous from the axioms present since order completeness landed (rr-sup-in / rr-sup-upper / rr-sup-least, number-systems.scm): if NN had an upper bound it would have a least one, s = SUP(NN); s - 1 is then not an upper bound, so s - 1 < n for some natural n, so s < n + 1, and n + 1 is a natural. Not mechanised -- that is the driver this warrant is standing in for.

  • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.

  • comb-kk-in-fun -- warrant well-known: Each COMB-KK(R,x,y,m) is a total function ZZ -> CARR R: base is IF into {ONE,ZERO}; step is a sum of products of carrier elements. Induction on m.
  • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form.   • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form.   • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.
  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.
  • bt-one-in-carr -- warrant well-known: ring ONE lies in CARR.
  • comb-kk-0-0 -- warrant well-known: comb-kk-zero + IF(0=0) picks the then-branch ONE(R).
  • bt-succ-in-nn -- warrant well-known: succ closes NN.
  • bt-nn-in-zz -- warrant well-known: NN subset ZZ.
  • bt-sum-in-carr-zz -- warrant well-known: SUM over the NN indices of a ZZ-fn lands in CARR.
  • bt-lt-succ -- warrant well-known: n < succ n.
  • ring-power-zero -- warrant informal: mpow-zero: MPOW(m,x,0)=IDEN(m); the view's E|->ONE slot gives IDEN(COMMUTATIVE-RING-MULTIPLICATIVE-CM R)=(ONE R).

r-exp-neg (trust: well-known)

trusted code: ineq, crs, arith, sos -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

  • max-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(a)<h(c) => a<c<b (a strict max above equal endpoints is interior).
  • rr-prod-nonpos-pos -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v>0 forces u<=0.
  • rr-prod-nonpos-neg -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v<0 forces u>=0.
  • continuous-nonpos-right -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is <=0 on a right-neighborhood (th,bb) is <=0 at th (sign preservation under continuity / one-sided limit).
  • continuous-nonneg-left -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is >=0 at th.
  • min-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(c)<h(a) => a<c<b.

  • rr-midpoint-between -- warrant well-known: a<b => exists m with a<m<b.

  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

  • comb-kk-in-fun -- warrant well-known: Each COMB-KK(R,x,y,m) is a total function ZZ -> CARR R: base is IF into {ONE,ZERO}; step is a sum of products of carrier elements. Induction on m.
  • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form. Rigorous from the axioms present since order completeness landed (rr-sup-in / rr-sup-upper / rr-sup-least, number-systems.scm): if NN had an upper bound it would have a least one, s = SUP(NN); s - 1 is then not an upper bound, so s - 1 < n for some natural n, so s < n + 1, and n + 1 is a natural. Not mechanised -- that is the driver this warrant is standing in for.

  • bt-neg1-neg -- warrant well-known: -1 < 0.
  • bt-succ-minus-1 -- warrant well-known: succ n - 1 = n in ZZ.
  • comb-kk-above -- warrant well-known: k>m => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base k>0 => IF(k=0) is ZERO; step k>succ m => both k-1>m and k>m, ZERO by IH.
  • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.
  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.
  • bt-one-in-carr -- warrant well-known: ring ONE lies in CARR.
  • comb-kk-0-0 -- warrant well-known: comb-kk-zero + IF(0=0) picks the then-branch ONE(R).
  • bt-succ-in-nn -- warrant well-known: succ closes NN.
  • bt-nn-in-zz -- warrant well-known: NN subset ZZ.
  • bt-sum-in-carr-zz -- warrant well-known: SUM over the NN indices of a ZZ-fn lands in CARR.
  • bt-lt-succ -- warrant well-known: n < succ n.
  • ring-power-zero -- warrant informal: mpow-zero: MPOW(m,x,0)=IDEN(m); the view's E|->ONE slot gives IDEN(COMMUTATIVE-RING-MULTIPLICATIVE-CM R)=(ONE R).

  • rr-prod-nonpos-pos -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v>0 forces u<=0.
  • rr-prod-nonpos-neg -- warrant well-known: u*v<=0 with v<0 forces u>=0.
  • continuous-nonpos-right -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is <=0 on a right-neighborhood (th,bb) is <=0 at th (sign preservation under continuity / one-sided limit).
  • continuous-nonneg-left -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is >=0 at th.
  • min-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(c)<h(a) => a<c<b.
  • deriv-neg -- warrant reference: Derivative of -f is -f': f(x)-f(a)=phi(x)(x-a) gives (-f)(x)-(-f)(a) = (-phi)(x)(x-a), with -phi continuous at a and value -L.
  • rr-midpoint-between -- warrant well-known: a<b => exists m with a<m<b.
  • diff-value-real -- warrant informal: IS-DIFF-AT's definition includes (IN L RR) as a conjunct.
  • cont-agree-off-pt -- warrant well-known: fa, fb continuous at pt and fa(x)=fb(x) for all x/=pt => fa(pt)=fb(pt). pt is a limit point of RR (no isolated points), so both values are the common limit of the punctured values; take x -> pt.
  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

  • comb-kk-in-fun -- warrant well-known: Each COMB-KK(R,x,y,m) is a total function ZZ -> CARR R: base is IF into {ONE,ZERO}; step is a sum of products of carrier elements. Induction on m.
  • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form. Rigorous from the axioms present since order completeness landed (rr-sup-in / rr-sup-upper / rr-sup-least, number-systems.scm): if NN had an upper bound it would have a least one, s = SUP(NN); s - 1 is then not an upper bound, so s - 1 < n for some natural n, so s < n + 1, and n + 1 is a natural.   • bt-succ-minus-1 -- warrant well-known: succ n - 1 = n in ZZ.
  • comb-kk-above -- warrant well-known: k>m => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base k>0 => IF(k=0) is ZERO; step k>succ m => both k-1>m and k>m, ZERO by IH.
  • nn-not-le-succ-le -- warrant well-known: NN is totally ordered and discrete: not(m<=n) gives n<m, hence succ n <= m.
  • co-le-trans -- warrant well-known: a<=b then b<=c gives a<=c.

  • bt-nn-in-zz -- warrant well-known: NN subset ZZ.
  • bt-sum-in-carr-zz -- warrant well-known: SUM over the NN indices of a ZZ-fn lands in CARR.
  • bt-lt-succ -- warrant well-known: n < succ n.
  • ring-power-zero -- warrant informal: mpow-zero: MPOW(m,x,0)=IDEN(m); the view's E|->ONE slot gives IDEN(COMMUTATIVE-RING-MULTIPLICATIVE-CM R)=(ONE R).

  • continuous-nonneg-left -- warrant well-known: A function continuous at th that is >=0 on a left-neighborhood (aa,th) is >=0 at th.
  • min-val-strict-interior -- warrant well-known: c in [a,b], h(a)=h(b), h(c)<h(a) => a<c<b.
  • deriv-neg -- warrant reference: Derivative of -f is -f': f(x)-f(a)=phi(x)(x-a) gives (-f)(x)-(-f)(a) = (-phi)(x)(x-a), with -phi continuous at a and value -L.
  • rr-midpoint-between -- warrant well-known: a<b => exists m with a<m<b.
  • diff-value-real -- warrant informal: IS-DIFF-AT's definition includes (IN L RR) as a conjunct.
  • cont-agree-off-pt -- warrant well-known: fa, fb continuous at pt and fa(x)=fb(x) for all x/=pt => fa(pt)=fb(pt). pt is a limit point of RR (no isolated points), so both values are the common limit of the punctured values; take x -> pt.
  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

TWO THINGS BLOCK THE MECHANIZATION, and neither is the mathematics.   • comb-kk-null -- warrant well-known: k<0 => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base IF(k=0) is ZERO for k<0; step xval(k-1)+yval(k) with k-1<0 and k<0 both ZERO by IH.
  • rr-le-scale-nonneg-right -- warrant well-known: x<=y and 0<=c give xc<=yc (multiply a non-strict inequality on the right by a nonnegative factor; the right-multiply form of rr-le-scale-nonneg).
  • nn-unbounded-in-rr -- warrant informal: NN is unbounded in RR: no real number is an upper bound for the naturals. The archimedean property, in its primary form. Rigorous from the axioms present since order completeness landed (rr-sup-in / rr-sup-upper / rr-sup-least, number-systems.scm): if NN had an upper bound it would have a least one, s = SUP(NN); s - 1 is then not an upper bound, so s - 1 < n for some natural n, so s < n + 1, and n + 1 is a natural. Not mechanised -- that is the driver this warrant is standing in for.

  • comb-kk-above -- warrant well-known: k>m => COMB-KK(.,m)(k)=ZERO. Induction on m: base k>0 => IF(k=0) is ZERO; step k>succ m => both k-1>m and k>m, ZERO by IH.

trusted code: arith, crs, ineq -- decision procedures, sound on their domain but believed rather than checked; they leave no leaf below.

proven modulo:

  • rr-is-normed-field -- warrant well-known: RR is a normed field under abs. Eight of the nine conjuncts of the IS-NORMED-FIELD IFF are the field and order axioms of number-systems.scm, discharged exactly as theorem-library/zz-ring-is-ring.scm discharges the six-slot IS-RING for ZZ-RING and QQ-RING: unfold the defining IFF, drop the accessors to the surface operations (binplus/bintimes/binneg/0/1), and cite rr-add-assoc / rr-add-comm / rr-add-zero / rr-neg-inverse / rr-mul-assoc / rr-mul-comm / rr-one-mul / rr-distributive. The ninth is is-norm(abs, ...), whose four value clauses are PROVEN, in theorem-library/rr-abs-basics.scm: rr-abs-nonneg (0 <= |a|), rr-abs-zero (|a| = 0 iff a = 0), rr-abs-mult (|ab| = |a||b|) and rr-abs-triangle (|a+b| <= |a| + |b|).

TWO THINGS BLOCK THE MECHANIZATION, and neither is the mathematics. (1) is-norm's FIRST conjunct is abs in FUN(CARR, RR)' -- membership in a function SPACE, not the pointwise typing rr-abs-closed gives. abs' is a primitive operator, i.e. a class function; that its restriction to RR is a SET is a replacement/sethood obligation, and nothing in the tree states it for abs (nor for `magnitude', which puts cc-is-normed-field in exactly the same position). (2) LOAD ORDER: rr-abs-basics.scm is a theorem-library file and loads some 900 entries after this one, so the proof cannot live where the axiom is cited from; retiring the axiom means moving the citation site, the way zz-is-integral-domain was moved.

sequential-implies-continuous-at (trust: informal)

proven modulo:

  • nn-recip-succ-pos -- warrant informal: 1/(n+1) is a positive real for every natural n. Rigorous from the axioms present, hence informal' rather than well-known': n + 1 >= 1 > 0 in RR (nn-in-rr and the order axioms), recip of a nonzero real is real (rr-recip-closed), and it is positive because a positive reciprocal is forced by a * recip a = 1 (rr-recip-inverse) together with rr-leq-mul-nonneg. Not mechanised: it needs recip-order lemmas the tree does not have yet.
  • nn-recip-succ-small -- warrant informal: For every eps > 0 there is a natural n with 1/(n+1) < eps. The corollary of nn-unbounded-in-rr that eps-arguments actually consume: apply unboundedness to x = 1/eps to get n > 1/eps, hence n + 1 > 1/eps > 0, hence 1/(n+1) < eps by antitonicity of recip on the positives. A rigorous paper proof exists from nn-unbounded-in-rr plus the ordered-field axioms, hence `informal'; mechanising it needs the recip-monotonicity lemmas (0 < a => 0 < recip a; 0 < a < b => recip b < recip a), which the tree does not have. Adding those two and proving this would trade one assertion for two, so it was deliberately not done -- see the note in separable.scm.

(i) cov(k) is a finite cover of PTS(s): image of the finite F_k is finite, and IS-R-NET makes every p in PTS(s) lie within rad(k) of some c in F_k, i.e. p in BALL(s,c,rad k) in cov(k) (IS-R-NET uses d<r, matching the open ball, so the balls truly cover). (ii) every member is by construction BALL(s,c,rad k) with c in F_k subset PTS(s) (centres in PTS(s) by DIST(s) typing). Also hands back (PTS s) in SET (free from IS-METRIC-SPACE s), the set V the combinatorial engine needs. No relation-set encoding -- nxt(k,u) is the successor SET, supplied as a VNB-LAMBDA, so callers avoid the (LIST k u y)-in-R comprehension/sethood/NTH plumbing (O1 of archive/calculus-pre-rename/block-family-rederive.scm).
